title: incremental-consumption-release-cadence-playbook
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood's recommended release cadence, packaging, and SLO alignment for incremental product changes that affect consumption economics (pricing, credits, fidelity), runtime surface behavior (latency, batching, caching impact), and customer-visible feature gates. It codifies cadence patterns (micro, meso, macro releases), packaging rules, experimentation guardrails, and a standardized rollout checklist to minimize billing surprises and operational risk.

Context and motivation

As Redwood's product surface grows (variants, fidelity knobs, capacity tiers, and Optimize features), frequent lightweight changes provide customer value faster but increase risk: incorrect crediting, unexpected latency regressions, or surprising fidelity shifts. This playbook balances speed-to-customer with predictable economics and operational safety.

Goals

- Deliver incremental product changes safely with predictable billing impact.
- Ensure every consumption-impacting change carries a deterministic SLO and pricing outcome.
- Standardize telemetry and canarying so regressions are caught before broad rollout.
- Reduce manual effort in billing adjustments by making changes idempotent and reversible.

Definitions

- Micro release: small surface-area changes (API flag flips, telemetry labels, small UX toggles) deployed to <5% of traffic, daily–weekly cadence.
- Meso release: feature increments that affect routing/consumption (new fidelity profile, quantization variant, modest pricing bundle changes) deployed to 10–30% of traffic, weekly–monthly cadence.
- Macro release: major platform changes (new consumption model, billing contract update, large variant rollout) staged over months with negotiated customer communication.

- Consumption-impacting change: any change that affects tokens billed, embedding storage, or adds/removes creditable features.
- Fidelity change: modifications that change output quality/compute required (e.g., quantization profile, attention head pruning).

Cadence patterns and rules

1) Micro releases
- Criteria: non-breaking API change, no billing schema changes, limited to configuration flips or small telemetry/UX updates.
- Rollout: immediate feature-flagged deployment to internal/dev accounts, 1% production canary for 24 hours, incremental increase to 5% over 72 hours if stable.
- Telemetry: ensure fine-grained metric tagging for the change (release_id, variant_id, experiment_id).
- Billing: no billing rule changes; if a micro-change changes per-request token count by >2%, treat as meso.

2) Meso releases
- Criteria: potential to change consumption signatures (fidelity, quantization, per-token compute), or new priced feature in Optimize/Console.
- Rollout: staged canary 5% → 15% → 30% over 2–4 weeks with automatic rollback triggers on SLO or cost anomalies.
- Pricing: attach exact consumption simulation (offline estimator run) with expected delta range and a migration window where customers see both old and new consumption.

3) Macro releases
- Criteria: changes to pricing models, contract-level SLAs, or surface-area changes that require customer action.
- Rollout: multi-month phased rollout with customer communication plan, migration tooling, and opt-in waves.

SLO alignment and rollback triggers

All rollout waves must define the following SLOs and automatic rollback conditions before deployment:

- Availability SLO: 99.95% regionally, 99.9% globally for new surface changes (measured rolling 7d).
- Latency SLO (generation endpoints): p95 ≤ 250ms for standard text-256 token baseline; p99 ≤ 800ms.
- Cost delta alert: automatic halt when observed per-token GPU-cost estimate deviates from predicted by >20% for 3h.
- Quality regressions: measured by a small internal eval set (minimum 200 synthetic prompts) with automatic rollback when BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop >5% for 24h.

Telemetry and quality gates

- Mandatory telemetry tags: release_id, rollout_wave, model_variant, quant_profile, customer_tier.
- Real-time dashboards: release health (errors, latencies), cost delta, fidelity delta, and per-tenant consumption delta.
- Light-touch eval capture: run a daily job against a canonical prompt set; output must be stored and compared to baseline.

Pricing and packaging implications

- Experimental period pricing rule: all meso and micro releases that touch billing must include a 14–30 day experimental crediting rule so early adopters do not face unexpected charges.
- Migration credit window: when changing a priced feature, default 30-day migration credits applied to customers with >$1k monthly usage unless explicitly opted-out.

Table: sample packaging mapping

| Release type | Pricing impact allowed | Default customer communication | Credit window |
|--------------|-----------------------|------------------------------|---------------|
| Micro        | None                  | Release notes                | N/A           |
| Meso         | Minor (±10% cost)     | In-console banner + email    | 14 days       |
| Macro        | Major (>10%)          | Direct account outreach      | 30–90 days     |

Rollout checklist (required fields)

1) Pre-approval (product & billing): change description, predicted consumption delta, experiment plan, rollback criteria.
2) Engineering readiness: feature flags, telemetry tags, canary automation, dark-launch mode where applicable.
3) Observability: dashboards created, alert thresholds configured, automated smoke tests in staging and prod-canary.
4) Legal/compliance: check data residency or contract clauses for macro changes.
5) Customer comms: in-console banner content, support playbook, and KB article drafted.

Experimentation & A/B rules

- All meso and macro experiments must define a primary metric (cost-adjusted quality score) and at least one guardrail metric (latency, availability).
- Minimum statistical power: experiments must collect data for a minimum of 7 full days and 10k requests per variant unless product approves a shorter window.

Roles and ownership

- Release owner (Product): coordinates pre-approval, executes communication plan, signs off on migration credits.
- Platform lead (Eng Platform): responsible for canary automation, flags, and real-time rollback hooks.
- Billing liaison (Finance): validates crediting rules and billing simulations.
- Observability owner (Eng SRE): creates dashboards and defines alerting thresholds.

Emergency rollback playbook

1) Detection: alert triggers (latency, error-rate, cost delta), or CS escalations.
2) Immediate action: engage release owner and platform lead, flip feature-flag to previous stable state, enable fallback routing to compatibility variant.
3) Post-incident: hot postmortem within 48 hours, billing reconciliation for affected customers, and permanent fix plan.

Communication templates (short)

- Console banner (Meso): "We're rolling out an optimization that may change per-request cost slightly for a subset of customers. If you'd like to opt out, visit [link]."
- Support KB excerpt: purpose, expected impact, how to opt out, contact escalation path.

Open questions and risks

- How to quantify fidelity delta for multimodal variants in an automated, comparable way?
- Pricing friction: customers on third-party marketplaces may require separate migration timelines.
- Long-tail tenants with spiky usage may be invisible in sample-based telemetry; need additional sampling heuristics.

Appendix A — Example 6-week meso rollout timeline

Week 0: Design + billing simulation + pre-approval.
Week 1: Internal canary and staging validation; create dashboards.
Week 2: 5% production canary (48–72h).
Week 3: 15% wave, collect 1 week of telemetry.
Week 4: 30% wave, collect 1 week of telemetry; run expanded eval set.
Week 5: 60% wave with optional migration credit enabled.
Week 6: Full rollout and finalize documentation + deprecation notes (if any).

Appendix B — Short checklist for Billing simulation (what to run)

- Run offline traffic-replay for a representative 14-day window.
- Compute per-tenant token delta and aggregate percentiles (median, p90, p99).
- Estimate per-tenant unit cost change using current GPU cost models.
- Produce a CSV with tenant_id, baseline_cost, predicted_cost, delta_pct for Finance sign-off.

Appendix C — Example alert rules (RFC)

- alert: ReleaseLatencyRegression
  expr: increase(p95_latency{release_id="<id>"}[1h]) > 1.2
  for: 30m
  action: pause-rollout

- alert: ReleaseCostDelta
  expr: avg_over_time(predicted_per_token_cost_delta{release_id="<id>"}[3h]) > 0.20
  for: 3h
  action: pause-rollout and require manual review

Notes and next steps

- Product should pilot this playbook with two upcoming meso releases in Q4 2029.
- Engineering to provide canary automation SDK and a reusable billing-sim job for self-serve runs.

Authored by Jordan Patel (Product) — draft for review by the release council.
